newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Gilts eye further gains while 112-12 holds.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Gilts eye further gains while 112-12 holds.

text.p: LIFFE June gilt futures' firmer close on Tuesday after an initial fall may have paved the way for further gains on Wednesday. But technical analysts had not yet cleared the contract for a sustained rally.
"It range-traded yesterday and then later it broke higher. While its over 112-12, it's best to stick with the trend," said Lynn Branigan, technical analyst at MCM Yieldwatch in London.
At 0700 GMT the June contract opened 5/32 higher on the day at 112-17.
Branigan said if gilts could hold above Tuesday's close of 112-12 they had a chance of capturing 112-18 and 112-26/30.

Initial resistance at 112-18 came from the high on Friday, while 112-26 represented a 38.2 percent retracement of contract highs down to Thursday's 111-21. Further up, 112-30 marked the start of the latest plunge.
Other upside hurdles would be provided by the 50 percent retracement of the move from contract highs at 113-07, then 113-19 which for now would be the maximum correction, Branigan said.

Gilts have pushed lower in the last two weeks, surrendering most of the gains racked up through an aggressive rally in early May when the Bank of England was given discretion on interest rate changes.
Branigan said failure to hold 112-12 could mean a test of 111-21, the May 22 low. Intermediate support is at 112-02.
Some analysts reckon any further signs of weakening could expose the gilt contract to the low of 111-02 touched on May 6.

"While prices have continued to rally from this area (111-26) over the last few days, a move that can be extended over the short term towards 112-20, we feel further selling pressure can develop over the next few days, to take the market closer to the 111-00 region," said HSBC Futures in London in a research note.
"The pullbacks continue to offer selling opportunities."
By 0738 GMT September short sterling was down 0.02 at 93.15.
